record.what_it_does: Customer support helpdesk and CRM suite: tickets, help center, messaging, AI agents.
record.auth_notes: OAuth access tokens (Bearer) are the standard method. Global OAuth tokens are required to distribute an app to multiple Zendesk customers. API tokens (email/token via Basic auth) are labeled deprecated and the docs recommend OAuth. End-user auth also exists. Auth is per Zendesk subdomain.
record.access_notes: A free 14-day trial gives a dev instance, so building and testing is self-serve. A sponsored account is for developer partners only. Distributing to many customers needs a global OAuth client, which I believe needs Zendesk review or registration. The page I fetched did not say this, and the setup guide was not opened. Production use needs a paid Zendesk plan. The API is available on most plans, but rate limits and some features vary by plan.
record.api_breadth_notes: Support/Ticketing API covers tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows. Other APIs cover Help Center/Guide, Messaging, Sunshine and others. Well over 100 endpoints in total.
record.mcp_notes: Zendesk announced an official MCP Server, with early access planned for summer 2026. Per search results, only the MCP Client was in early access at the time of that announcement, and I did not confirm that the server is GA or has a hosted URL. Third-party servers exist: Workato, Redpanda, Merge, StackOne, fruggr/zendesk-mcp-server, and a Swifteq Marketplace app.
record.blocker_notes: Per-subdomain OAuth is easy to build against on a free trial. Public multi-tenant distribution needs a global OAuth client, which may involve Zendesk approval. Sandboxes are Enterprise-only, though the 14-day trial works for dev. Each end user's Zendesk subdomain must be collected.
